name: Guardian genius crossword No 268
preamble: Wordplay in each across clue generates an extra letter that doesn’t belong in the grid; in order these letters should lead the solver to a thematic modification of a single word in each down clue. The unclued down entry is thematic.

clue.text: One's cutting with praise, craftily

indicators.note: done craftily, the letters of praise and the with-letter are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
the word itself supplies letters, less the E that is this clue's extra letter

explanation.surface: Someone flatters the boss with cunning, and the flattery is itself a kind of cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumble yields seven letters; the spare E is this clue's extra letter for the message, and is not entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripsaw is a coarse saw for cutting wood along the grain, so it is the thing doing the cutting.

clue.text: Correct to cycle on hard local seaweed close to land

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

blocks.note: the clue's swapped word: Correct stands in for Wrong, whose synonym is sin
H is the pencil-lead grading for hard
ore is a dialect word for seaweed

explanation.surface: Instructions to bike along a shore where the seaweed is slippery.
explanation.walkthrough: Correct has traded places with Wrong in 19 Down; read Wrong here, giving SIN, whose last letter moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore waters lie near the coast, so inshore means near the land.

clue.text: Wealthy new theatre's deserted

definitions.note: the swapped word, standing for broke, the past tense of break, as shattered is

indicators.note: new letters are a fresh arrangement of the old ones

blocks.note: the word with its S supplies the letters to be rearranged
D is a recorded abbreviation for deserted

explanation.surface: A rich man's new playhouse stands empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Wealthy has traded places with broke in 23 Down: read Broke, which as a verb means shattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke and shattered both describe glass breaking into pieces, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: In contest win exhausted horse

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the conflict
an exhausted word is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

blocks.note: war is a contest of arms
the swapped word: win stands in for lose, its opposite

explanation.surface: A worn-out horse still wins its race.
explanation.walkthrough: Win has traded places with lose in 15 Down, so read lose here. A waler is an Australian saddle horse, first bred in New South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The waler is a breed of horse from New South Wales, prized as a cavalry mount.

clue.text: Soldier and doctor circling mine, for example

indicators.note: the doctor's two letters go around the mine's letters, one on each side

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
DM is Doctor of Medicine, the Oxford form of the degree
to dig is to mine

explanation.surface: A paratrooper and a medic surround a landmine, the sort of scene a training manual offers as a case study.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives PARADDIGM; the spare D is the extra letter for the message.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a model or typical instance, a pattern that others follow.

clue.text: [Not clued]
Again picks lesser canine, oddly lacking height somehow

indicators.note: losing the odd letters leaves the second and fourth
somehow says the letters arrive in some new order

blocks.note: the word itself goes into the mix
C stands for a canine tooth in dental notation
the swapped word: height stands in for its opposite, depth

explanation.surface: A dog breeder again chooses the smaller hound, strangely lacking in stature.
explanation.walkthrough: Height has traded places with depth in 25 Down. Dentists chart teeth as I, C, P and M: incisor, canine, premolar, molar.
explanation.definitionFit: To reselect is to select once more, so reselects means picks a second time.

clue.text: Up in the first half but floundering in uncertainty

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is kept
floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters of but tumble

blocks.note: the swapped word: Up stands in for its opposite, Down
the word itself supplies the letters to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A team is ahead at half-time but then founders, leaving the result in question.
explanation.walkthrough: Up has traded places with down in 17 Down, so read Down here.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubt is a state of being unsure, the same thing as uncertainty.

clue.text: Smirk provided by pleasant afternoon these days

blocks.note: the swapped word: pleasant stands in for harsh, whose synonym is grim
A is a short form for afternoon in timetables
CE is the Common Era, the present era

explanation.surface: A smug smile prompted by a lovely modern afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Pleasant has traded places with harsh in 21 Down, so read harsh here.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression, and Chambers counts an affected smirk among them.

clue.text: A special project with German aggressor
Movie producer's exercise in art: The First Love

blocks.note: a study is a practice piece made by an artist
I is the regnal numeral of a first monarch, as in Elizabeth I
love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A painter's practice sketch is presented as the opening romance of some saga.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y of the study is the extra letter for the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Film studios are the companies that make and release movies, so a studio is a movie producer.

clue.text: Retired professor put on weight for nothing

indicators.note: retired here means withdrawn backwards, so the academic's title runs the other way

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher
WT is the usual abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: An emeritus academic has piled on pounds and got nothing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives NODWT; the spare D is the extra letter. NOWT is northern English dialect for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowt is the dialect word for nothing, the counterpart of owt meaning anything.

clue.text: Neural convulsing of kidneys

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective renal

indicators.note: a convulsion throws things into disorder, so the letters of neural are reshuffled

blocks.note: the word itself supplies the letters, less the U that is this clue's extra letter

explanation.surface: A medical note about nerve spasms affecting the kidneys.
explanation.walkthrough: Six letters are rearranged into five; the spare U is the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the medical adjective relating to the kidneys, from Latin renes.

clue.text: Cause pain to the heartless chest

indicators.note: a word without its heart keeps only its outside letters

blocks.note: the word itself, before its middle letter is removed
an ark is a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Something wounds the uncaring torso, a pain with no feeling behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of the ark is the extra letter. To tear is to rend or lacerate, hence to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear flesh or feelings is to wound, so tearing is a way of inflicting pain.

clue.text: Tailless bird in river for 60 minutes

definitions.note: a singular measure, as degree is

indicators.note: the shortened bird sits inside the river's name

blocks.note: the Dee is a river of Wales and England, and of Scotland
an egret, the white heron, with its last letter cut off

explanation.surface: A bird missing its tail swims in a river for an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sixty minutes is not an hour here but a degree of arc. The wordplay gives DEGREEE, and the spare E is the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In angle measurement one degree divides into sixty minutes of arc.

clue.text: Starting late, lose elegant rambling rose

indicators.note: starting late means the first letter is missed
a rambling rose sprawls, and so do these letters

blocks.note: the swapped word: lose stands in for its opposite, win
the word itself goes into the mix

explanation.surface: A gardener's lament: an elegant climbing rose that flowered late.
explanation.walkthrough: Lose has traded places with win in 4 Down, so read win here. Rambling looks like a type of rose; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: Bouncer — doorman, essentially — in charge briefly of strongbox

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: the seven-letter word, whose central letter is wanted
I/C is the short form of in charge
O stands for of, as in o'clock
a chest is a box for valuables

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer, the man on the door, is put in charge of the safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouncer suggests a doorman, which the clue then names, but it means something that bounces off. The S of the chest is the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is a shot or object rebounding off a surface, something that bounces.

clue.text: Saddler perhaps can't initially settle farm down

definitions.note: a saddler is one example of a skilled tradesman

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of settle
the swapped word: down stands in for up, which signals letters in disarray

blocks.note: the word itself, without its apostrophe, goes into the mix
the word whose first letter is taken
the word itself goes into the mix

explanation.surface: A saddler who cannot settle at first moves down to the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Down has traded places with Up in 7 Down, so read up here: letters that are up are in turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler makes saddles and harness by hand, an example of a skilled tradesman.

clue.text: Daring shop taking on hotel in walled city

indicators.note: the shop takes the hotel letter into itself

blocks.note: bold means daring
a deli is a delicatessen
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An enterprising store takes over a hotel inside an old fortified town.
explanation.walkthrough: The B of bold is the extra letter. Old Delhi is the historic walled city of Shahjahanabad in India's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Delhi, founded as Shahjahanabad, was enclosed by city walls with gates such as Kashmiri Gate.

clue.text: Wrong fish over in current moving with wind

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the swapped word: Wrong stands in for Correct, and to correct is to edit
the eel is a fish

explanation.surface: The wrong fish turns up in a current driven by the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrong has traded places with Correct in 2 Down, so read Correct here.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee tide is a tidal stream running the same way as the wind blows.

clue.text: Waitress finally arrived with epic shelled seafood

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the waitress
shelling a word strips off its outer letters, leaving the inside

blocks.note: the word whose last letter is taken
came means arrived
the word whose outer letters are stripped

explanation.surface: The waitress at last turns up with a huge platter of prawns already out of their shells.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of came is the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustine tails, usually served breaded, a classic British seafood dish.

clue.text: Head of harsh country has curtailed swimmer

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the swapped word: harsh stands in for its opposite, pleasant
Iran is the country
the word itself, before its last letter is docked

explanation.surface: The leader of a severe regime keeps a fish with a docked tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Harsh has traded places with pleasant in 8 Down, so read pleasant here.
explanation.definitionFit: The piranha is a South American river fish, famous for sharp teeth and swimming in shoals.

clue.text: In Bulgaria, money from rent very advanced

blocks.note: to let is to rent out
V is the abbreviation for very
A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: In Bulgaria the money from letting property is very high.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of let is the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The lev is Bulgaria's currency unit, and leva is its plural.

clue.text: Ultimately broke, after a fashion, leading to lack of energy

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter
the last letter is placed after the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
ton is fashion or style, from French
the swapped word: broke stands in for its opposite, wealthy

explanation.surface: Ending up penniless in a way that leaves one listless.
explanation.walkthrough: Broke has traded places with Wealthy in 3 Down, so read wealthy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Atony is the medical term for slackness or loss of tone in a muscle, a want of vigour.

clue.text: Newton, one collecting infrared iridescent material

indicators.note: the card takes the infrared letters into its middle

blocks.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
an ace is a one in cards
IR is the standard short form of infrared

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton, studying light, gathers infrared rays from a shimmering substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives NACIRE; the spare I is the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, the shimmering lining of oyster and abalone shells.

clue.text: Alcohol essentially thrown up, washing liquid limiting depth

indicators.note: in a down clue thrown up means read from the bottom, so the letters go backwards
the liquid surrounds the other letters, setting their limits

blocks.note: lye is an alkaline solution used for washing
the swapped word: depth stands in for height, abbreviated HT

explanation.surface: Someone drank too much and was sick, and the cleaning fluid barely covers it.
explanation.walkthrough: Depth has traded places with height in 6 Down, so read height here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl is the radical at the core of ordinary drinking alcohol, ethanol, or ethyl alcohol.

clue.text: Nine months? Three months!

blocks.note: a tern is a set of three, as in a lottery draw
M is the abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: A pregnancy lasts nine months, and a school term about three: two quick exclamations about time.
explanation.walkthrough: The N of tern is the extra letter. The question mark flags that nine months is a term only in the sense of a full pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnancy carried to term lasts about nine months, so term names that full span.

clue.text: On the counter, provided travel bag to carry duck dumplings

indicators.note: counter here means running the opposite way, so everything is read backwards
the bag carries the duck inside it

blocks.note: if means provided that
a grip is a holdall
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: At the shop counter, someone packs ducks into a holdall to take home some dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives PIROGFI; the spare F is the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirogi are Polish and Russian filled dumplings, also spelt pierogi.

clue.text: Cruel to bury entertaining Scotsman

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the Scot goes inside

blocks.note: inhume is a formal verb for bury
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a stock Scotsman

explanation.surface: It seems cruel to bury a Scot who is so amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives INHUMIANE; the spare I is the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane means lacking pity or compassion, the same quality as cruelty.

clue.text: Witch 'English Nelly' knocked back chemical

indicators.note: knocking something back sends it the other way, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: a hex is a witch, from the German Hexe
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A witch called English Nelly downs a chemical concoction.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal gives YLLENE; dropping the extra L leaves the chemical's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Hexylene is a hydrocarbon, an alkene with six carbon atoms, also called hexene.

clue.text: Latin writer is almost straightforward in terms of narrative

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin
the writer speaking of himself says I'm
near means almost, as in a near disaster

explanation.surface: A classical author is nearly plain in how he tells a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The M of I'm is the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A linear story runs in chronological order, without flashbacks or parallel threads.
